args.text:
Julio Teherán, a two-time Major League Baseball All-Star, has called time on his baseball career, announcing his retirement on Monday at the age of 35. The call came two days after he was pulled from a scheduled start for Team Colombia at the 2026 World Baseball Classic (WBC) with a crook shoulder.

Before he hung up the glove, Teherán had helped Team Colombia to a 3-1 win over Team Panama at the WBC.

Teherán had a thirteen-year MLB career, most of it with the Atlanta Braves, though he also had stints with the Los Angeles Angels, Detroit Tigers, Milwaukee Brewers and New York Mets. He made his MLB debut with the Braves in 2011 as a 20-year-old and stuck with them for his first nine seasons, picking up All-Star selections in 2014 and 2016.

All up, Teherán finished his MLB career with an 81-82 record, a 3.85 ERA, a 1.223 WHIP and 1,260 strikeouts in 1,470.2 innings. He'd also spent the 2022 and 2025 seasons in the Mexican Baseball League.
